newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins as freezing fears remain.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins as freezing fears remain.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds eased as the market remained overshadowed by news that more bonds may be frozen.
Dealers said trading was thinned by a UK bank holiday.
Russian police are preparing an order to freeze up to another nominal $7 million of MinFin bonds, which have been stolen, banking sources told Reuters on Friday.

"London operators are not working, and prices are steady as our banks are not ready to start a new trend," one dealer said. He added some banks had been trying to start a speculative buying spree but found no support.
Dealers said some Russian banks had left the market until the problem of new stolen bonds was cleared up.
"Some Russian banks have cut their positions although foreigners were buying quite actively late on Friday (after the news of possible freezing had appeared)," one dealer said.
He added prices could rise on Tuesday despite the generally negative impact from more bonds being frozen in the near future.

"The news is not so bad actually. The said amount is not so large if it is spread out evenly on the market. Somebody could start speculative selling, but there should be good support," another dealer said.
